Be part of an organisation driven by digital technology and data-backed approaches that support a diversified portfolio of prescription medicines, vaccines, and animal health products. Drive innovation and execution excellence. Be a part of a team with passion for using data, analytics, and insights to drive decision-making, and which creates custom software, allowing us to tackle some of the world's greatest health threats. Our Technology Centers focus on creating a space where teams can come together to deliver business solutions that save and improve lives. An integral part of our companys’ IT operating model, Tech Centers are globally distributed locations where each IT division has employees to enable our digital transformation journey and drive business outcomes. These locations, in addition to the other sites, are essential to supporting our business and strategy. A focused group of leaders in each Tech Center helps to ensure we can manage and improve each location, from investing in growth, success, and well-being of our people, to making sure colleagues from each IT division feel a sense of belonging to managing critical emergencies. Global collaboration This role will work closely with colleagues across the U.S. East Coast, Dublin (Ireland), Prague (Czech Republic), and Singapore technology centers. Experience 3+ years of relevant professional experience. OT/IT security background Experience designing and operating IT/OT cybersecurity controls for critical infrastructure systems. Firewall governance Experience reviewing and approving firewall rules, with a strong understanding of the security risks associated with data flows across segmented network zones. Shop floor / lab systems design review Experience reviewing real-time shop floor and laboratory system designs to ensure data flows meet appropriate security and resiliency requirements. Experience designing or supporting IT and OT systems for manufacturing and laboratory environments in the following domains Firewalls, Remote Access Management, Network security design & observability Execution mindset Results-oriented, with a demonstrated ability to develop plans and execute them successfully. Preferred Skills Broad understanding of IT and OT systems supporting Manufacturing & Supply Chain operations, including MES, quality and laboratory systems, resource planning systems, process control technologies, and cold chain / other supply chain systems. Intermediate understanding of industrial/OT security concepts and familiarity with relevant industry standards and guidance, such as NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-82, and related NIST publications. Working knowledge and practical application of the Purdue Model for network segmentation in industrial environments. Prior experience in the pharmaceutical industry is preferred. Entry-level cybersecurity certification (e.g., CEH, CompTIA, GISF, GSEC, or similar). Today, our company continues to be at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions and advance the prevention and treatment of diseases that threaten people and animals around the world. review_candidates.title: Senior System Engineer Robotics
review_candidates.description: Your mission Our robots don't ship with a robotics team standing next to them in the warehouse. They ship with NODE.OS, and NODE.OS is yours to own. Robotics Core pushes the algorithmic boundary in navigation, localization and planning. Frontier turns robot state into interfaces people actually trust. You sit between them and turn what they build into a robot that shows up for its shift, does its job, and doesn't page anyone at 3am. Not a hardware role: no motor drivers, no sourcing LiDAR units. Everything above that is yours, from the driver layer to a fleet of dozens moving through our Master Control System (VDA5050-compliant). You're not maintaining one module. You're accountable for how our robots perform in the field. What you'll do Sit between Robotics Core and Frontier: Their output becomes something operable, field reality becomes requirements they can act on. What's worth building and what's worth working around is your call. Own the driver-to-behavior stack: Hardware abstraction, ROS 2 DISTRO Jazzy driver layer, state machines. Where the line falls between a hardware quirk you abstract away and a behavior bug you fix properly is your decision, and every later feature inherits it. Design and guard the safety-relevant logic on the robot: Every rule trades throughput against certainty, and you own the trade-off, not just the code that implements it. Own robot-to-fleet communication: VDA5050 up to the Master Control System, plus the coordination and traffic-management logic that has to hold up on a real warehouse floor. The algorithms often come from Robotics Core, but when integration turns up gaps you dig into them instead of just wiring them up. Run the Master Control System as a production service: Cloud Deployed using Docker. Observability using OpenTelemetry, Orchestration open. You define what counts as a healthy fleet, and what triggers an alert versus a shrug. Own deployment and SRE for robot and fleet software: Every rollout strategy, rollback plan and monitoring threshold is a bet on how much operator trust you'll risk for speed. Debug production incidents on live customer fleets: Whether you call something a root cause or a symptom decides whether the same failure shows up again next week. Your profile Must-have 7+ yrs building and operating software for AMRs, or comparable safety-relevant real-time distributed systems ROS 2 or comparable, and you can reason about driver layers, state machines and behavior architectures C++ and/or Python, at a level where you know when correctness beats shipping speed Safety concepts in robotics or industrial systems: you design for the failure case, not the happy path Production distributed systems: pipelines, monitoring, incident response, rollback. You've been on-call for something that mattered You've owned a technical decision others disagreed with, and can still defend the trade-off You've carried something into production and stayed with it afterwards, including the part where it broke You question a requirement before you build it, without making the person who wrote it defensive Nice-to-have VDA5050 or other fleet-management standards Multi-robot coordination or traffic management Intralogistics, warehouse automation, industrial deployments Observability tooling, chaos and fault-injection thinking Not for you if you're early career or coming straight out of studies. No hard feelings, we just don't have the ramp-up capacity for this scope. What we offer Your rhythm matters most, which is why we don't do such a thing as core hours Hybrid Deutschland-Ticket, subsidised Urban Sports Club Learning budget a year, spend it on whatever moves you Corporate Benefits for exclusive discounts …and of course plenty of snacks and drinks in the office

review_candidates.description: About Nebius Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The role We are seeking a highly technical and experienced Network Planning Technical Project Manager to join our infrastructure team. In this pivotal role, you will be the bridge between internal data center development teams and external telecommunications partners. You will own the connectivity lifecycle—from initial site opportunity assessment through to the final Outside Plant infrastructure delivery—ensuring our facilities are seamlessly integrated into the global network. The ideal candidate possesses a deep understanding of fiber optics, ISP commercial structures, and geospatial data management, coupled with the project management discipline to drive complex, multi-stakeholder builds across the region. Optical Networking: Strong grasp of DWDM technology, ILA requirements, and the technical lifecycle of MOFN deployments. Relationship Management: Proven ability to influence stakeholders and external vendors to meet aggressive regional deployment timelines. review_candidates.title: Co-Founder - Head of Credit & Structured Finance
review_candidates.description: What NuruFi does? NuruFi is the credit engine for clean energy trade in emerging markets. We operate an asset-light risk verification and assessment engine that enables clean energy equipment distributors to safely extend credit terms to local EPCs, unlocking stalled pipelines and getting productive-use solar assets into the market faster. The trajectory is phased: v1 asset-light underwriting and servicing (earn fees, build the dataset); v2 tooling to make assessment faster and cheaper; v3 financing purchase orders directly, funded by a separate debt vehicle raised once the performance record justifies it. The core capability is underwriting productive-use payers that carry no credit rating and that international funds cannot assess cost-effectively NuruFi is currently part of the Carbon13 venture-building programme. The current team: Founder / CEO — energy systems engineer; owns the technical underwriting (system design, sizing, performance risk) and overall direction. Operations & Credit Lead (Uganda) — origination, on-the-ground verification, and collections. The role: You would own credit as a function and build it into a system. Specifically: Underwriting. Own and develop the credit methodology — the scorecard, risk framework, and decisioning — for unrated business payers. Personally assess deals in the early phase; the manual work is the point, and it is how the model gets built. Structuring. Set deal terms (limits, tenor, deposits, milestones), design the collection waterfall, and work with local counsel on assignment of receivables and its perfection. Portfolio & risk. Build servicing, monitoring, early-warning, and workout/recovery practice. Own the performance dataset that the underwriting model will be trained and re-weighted against. Capital (as the company matures). Lead the eventual raise of a debt facility and the relationships with debt funds, DFIs, and guarantors that finance the receivables in the next phase. Co-Founder Governance: Participate directly in company strategy, investor fundraising pitches, board dynamics, and institutional scaling. Who you are? Direct experience underwriting SME, trade, receivables, or working-capital credit in an African or emerging market — you have made real credit decisions and lived with the outcomes. Hands-on. You are willing to assess deals yourself, chase payments, and work out a default in the early stage, not only design frameworks for others to run. Comfortable building structure from little: a scorecard in a spreadsheet before it is a system; a method before it is software. Working knowledge of structured trade finance and debt-raising — receivables facilities, security and collateral, and what debt funds and DFIs require — or a credible path to owning it. Grounded and analytical in how you communicate risk. Numbers and structure over narrative. Useful: Exposure to clean-energy, asset, or equipment finance. Familiarity with East African legal and payments infrastructure (movable-collateral registration, mobile money, bank rails, assignment of receivables). A network among debt funds, DFIs, or guarantee providers active in Sub-Saharan Africa. Terms: Co-founder equity, commensurate with a founding role and the stage. Cash compensation is limited until the first raise, which this role helps lead. Equity: Co-Founder Equity Share (12% – 20%, vesting schedule, open to negotiation based on experience and capital match capability)
